cards.explanation: The answer is False. The writer says, “For it is not to angels that He has subjected the world to come…” (Hebrews 2:5). It's a flat no on the angels, friends. The world to come is not put under them.

The answer is True. The psalm says, “You made him a little lower than the angels…” (Hebrews 2:7). A LITTLE lower, not a lot lower. And look at what comes next: “You crowned him with glory and honor” (Hebrews 2:7).

The answer is nothing, bakers! The writer says, “When God subjected all things to him, He left nothing outside of his control.” (Hebrews 2:8). Not one thing got left off the list. That's about as thorough as someone who checks every single oven twice.

The answer is True, and the writer is honest about it. He says, “Yet at present we do not see everything subject to him.” (Hebrews 2:8). He doesn't pretend otherwise, friends. Neither will I. My own bakery doesn't always listen to me either.

The answer is because He suffered death, friends. The writer says Jesus is “…now crowned with glory and honor because He suffered death…” (Hebrews 2:9). The reason is right there in the verse. This is a heavy part, so I'll let those words sit for a second.

The answer is many sons, friends. The writer says God is “…bringing many sons to glory…” (Hebrews 2:10). Jesus is the author of their salvation, and God is the one bringing them. Many, bakers. Not a small batch.

The answer is suffering, friends. The writer says it was fitting for God “…to make the author of their salvation perfect through suffering.” (Hebrews 2:10). That's a heavy line, and I think it deserves a quiet moment. It's the word the verse uses, and we can trust it.

The answer is True. The writer says, “For both the One who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are of the same family.” (Hebrews 2:11). So Jesus and the people He sanctifies belong to one family, friends. Same family. No awkward introductions needed at the door.

The answer is brothers, bakers! The verse says, “So Jesus is not ashamed to call them brothers.” (Hebrews 2:11). Jesus and the people He sanctifies are one family, so He calls them brothers. Not ashamed. I'd put that on a tea towel, but my mustache can't sew.

The answer is God's name, friends. In this quote, Jesus speaks to God, and He says, “I will proclaim Your name to My brothers…” (Hebrews 2:12). The name is what He says He'll proclaim. I think that's a sweet thing to promise His brothers.

The answer is the devil, friends. The writer says Jesus shared in our humanity so that by His death He might destroy “…him who holds the power of death, that is, the devil…” (Hebrews 2:14). The writer names him outright. So there's no guessing about who it is.

The answer is death, bakers. The verse says Jesus would “…free those who all their lives were held in slavery by their fear of death.” (Hebrews 2:15). All their lives, friends. I think a fear that long would feel heavy to carry.

The answer is False. The writer says, “For surely it is not the angels He helps, but the descendants of Abraham.” (Hebrews 2:16). Angels are great, friends, but they aren't who this verse says He helps.

The answer is a high priest, friends. The verse says Jesus was made like His brothers so “…He might become a merciful and faithful high priest in service to God…” (Hebrews 2:17). Merciful and faithful, both together. That's two good words right in a row.

The answer is those who are being tempted, friends. The writer says, “Because He Himself suffered when He was tempted, He is able to help those who are being tempted.” (Hebrews 2:18). Jesus knows what it's like. I think that's a good thing to hold onto on a rough day.
